questions.answer: The nature

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the UiBs website has a very pedagodical guide that I used prior to and during my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really that much. The UiB administration was very helpfull if there was any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I am not sure if I was just lucky, but I found a nice shared appartment in the middle of downtown. Most of my friends also found their own housing in and around the city. I recomend using Hybel for looking for accomodation. Just start looking in proper time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I do not think one semester studentens can live close to campus anyways. Basically everythnig is very close, but it could be nice to find something close to your specific campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To be honest I do not even really remember the process, which just speaks to the simplicity.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The UiBstreet, studentweb (internal systems) and the UiB website all gave plenty of information. And if I was ever in any doubt the administration was quick to respond to mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succsesful. I didn't get two courses I wanted to eroll in but that was due to very valid reasons. The one was reserved for first year biologist student and was not offered for exchange. The second was a sub-courses mangled in a larger masters track, so it made sense they couldn't offer it to me. I gpt all other courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep order in all the important mails you get, and save links to webpages you need to access later. It can quickly turn confusing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to what I am used to in UCPH. However, I have a block structure and even though the courses spanned a whole semester, they felt very much just like a slightly longer block. That is to say that prehaps the levels was not that hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very refreshing and creative. I can't, of course, speak on the behalf of all courses but the ones I had applied a variety of teaching styles. Lectures, excurtions, poster sessions, gruops work and presentations where some of the methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIO203 - Introduction to aquaculture
BIO201 - From individual to ecosystem
BIO250 - Palaeoecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Palaeoecology was a great course with a subject matter not discussed much in the basic curriculum at UCPH. The course included both an excurstion with field work, lab work and a poster session. Great course, the only caveat is that it is only held every other year.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I tried to buy a bike twice, and they both got stolen within the week I got them... so yeah, don't buy a bike.
Other than that you might buy some extra hiking gear if you don't already have it.
Also, If you want to workout the sammen GYms are great and quite cheap, but you have to pay for the whole semester up front (around 1000dkk).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Genereally I think that the food prices are exaggereated. On avarage I belive the price of groceries are around 10-20% more expensive, but it really depends on what you buy. I recommend using the "eTilbudsavis" for scouting out deals. The Rema1000 app is also a must, but it should be noted that it is regionlocked and needs a Norwegian number to work. This can be a bit tricky but the special deals you unlock are definetly worth it.
Also try not to eat out to much, but if you do byVENN are good for deals.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are many activities happening in Bergen all the time. It is a very dynamic city, especially if you volenteer e.g. Spire, Hulen, are the ecco festival.
Honestly I mostly just went hiking every weekend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, the nature is breathtaking. Otherwise refer to my answer to previos question.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I can not overstate just how amazing the nature is. Try to maximize your time in nature.
use the "UT" app to get the locations of cabins and trails.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As a dansih person there is hardly any difference between our cultures, it honestly almost felt like going to a different region in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Learning the language was a fun challenge.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-Find your own accomodation, preferably with Norwegian people.
-Maximize hiking, get a memberhip with DNT (Den Norske Tursitforening) that makes cabins a whole lot cheaper.
- Don't get a bike, they will be stolen. Trust.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When planning hikes public transportation can proce tricky over the weekends. If possible shift the trips to enable transportation on weekdays. Otherwise renting cars are pretty affordable if you are multiple that shares. Hyre is a great service get the Hyre pass if renting often this saves a lot of money (If you swith your location in the app to norway you get the pass cheaper only 99 NOK).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences I got outdoors. Especially on my solo trips, they were truly eyeopening. But also trips with friends, going for morning swims in mountain lakes and making food with storm kitchens next to waterfalls.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly back home I can find it hard to balance my sudy load, which has lead to something akin to burnout in the past. It took some geting used to to prioritize the culture, nature and people a bit more than back home. But definetly wort it, and remeber that your grades won't get transferred;)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
